papers.title: Model-embedded Gaussian Process Regression for Parameter Estimation and Uncertainty Quantification in Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: The identification of dynamical systems is a vital task in science and engineering. Traditional methods require numerous calls to the dynamical-system solver, rendering likelihood-based or least-squares inference frameworks impractical. For efficient parameter inference, two state-of-the-art techniques are the kernel method for modeling and the one-step framework for jointly inferring unknown parameters and hyperparameters. The kernel method is a quick and straightforward technique, but it cannot estimate solutions and their derivatives, which must strictly adhere to physical laws. We propose a model-embedded one-step Bayesian framework for joint inference of unknown parameters and hyperparameters by maximizing the marginal likelihood. This approach models the solution and its derivatives using Gaussian process regression (GPR), taking into account smoothness and continuity properties, and treats differential equations as constraints that can be naturally integrated into the Bayesian framework in the linear case. Additionally, we prove convergence of the model-embedded Gaussian process regression (ME-GPR) for theoretical development. Motivated by Taylor expansion, we introduce a piecewise first-order linearization strategy to handle nonlinear dynamical systems. Numerical experiments on simulated linear and nonlinear dynamical systems evaluate the method’s performance in parameter estimation and in predicting solutions and their derivatives.

papers.title: A hybrid digital twin framework for friction stir welding integrating multi-physics simulation, sensor data, and machine learning
papers.abstract: Friction stir welding (FSW) is a solid-state joining process capable of producing high-quality, high-strength joints without material melting. However, the strong sensitivity of FSW to process parameters, material variations, and operational disturbances often leads to inconsistent weld quality, creating challenges for reliable industrial quality assurance. Although finite element simulations and experimental optimization studies have improved understanding of underlying thermo-mechanical behavior, most existing approaches remain offline and lack the ability to adapt to real-time process variations. This study presents a comprehensive digital twin framework for FSW by integrating multi-physics finite element simulations, real-time multi-sensor data acquisition, and machine-learning-based predictive analytics. The finite element model captures key physical phenomena, including heat transfer, material flow, and residual stress evolution during welding of AA6061-T6 aluminum alloy, providing a robust physics-based baseline. Real-time synchronization is achieved through thermal, force, and vibration sensor data, enabling continuous updating of the virtual model to reflect process disturbances such as tool wear and clamping variability. Machine learning models are embedded within the digital twin to enhance predictive capability. An artificial neural network predicts mechanical properties with a coefficient of determination (R²) exceeding 0.9, while a support vector machine classifier detects weld defects with accuracy above 92%. Experimental validation confirms that predicted tensile strength and hardness deviate by less than ±4% from measured values. The proposed framework enables real-time monitoring, predictive quality assurance, and proactive defect prevention, advancing friction stir welding toward intelligent, self-adaptive manufacturing aligned with Industry 4.0.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural network for temperature field prediction and multi-parameter inversion of early-age concrete
papers.abstract: Predicting concrete temperature is critical for controlling thermal cracking. However, traditional finite element (FE) models rely heavily on empirical parameters and boundary assumptions, which often deviate significantly from actual site conditions. To address this issue, this paper proposes a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for early-age temperature field prediction and parameter inversion. First, we establish a thermal-humidity coupling multiphysics FE model. Second, the heat conduction equation, equivalent age evolution, and moisture evaporation mechanisms are embedded as physical constraints into the loss function, constructing a PINN driven by on-site monitoring data. To address the severe ill-posedness of multi-parameter joint inversion, introduce the Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) and profile likelihood for identifiability analysis. This reveals strong parameter collinearity and motivates a dimension-reduction strategy that focuses inversion on core hydration parameters, with uncertainties quantified via Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC). Results show that the inverted parameters differ significantly from empirical values (21.1% and 6.5%). When fed back into an independent COMSOL model, the calibrated FE model reduces the early-stage (0- 48 h) temperature prediction MAE at key observation points by an average of 41.3%. Furthermore, temporal hold-out tests demonstrate the model's generalization capability by predicting unseen time windows (train 96 h) with an RMSE of 3.434°C, and spatial cross-validation yields robust predictions on unseen sensors. The model also maintains parameter stability under artificially injected sensor noise. This study provides a reliable data-physics fusion approach for rapid model calibration and early curing decision-making in engineering applications.

papers.title: Research on the control method of a loading device for machine tool accuracy retention testing
papers.abstract: Accuracy retention testing is an important means of evaluating the ability of machine tools to retain their accuracy. Actively applying dynamic loads to simulate actual cutting loads is a key part of these tests and enables quantitative investigation of their effects on machine tool accuracy. To accommodate the limited installation space inside a machine tool, a compact 3-degree-of-freedom (3-DOF) on-machine loading device based on a Delta parallel mechanism is developed to apply dynamic loads simultaneously in the X, Y, and Z directions to a vertical machining center. To compensate for loading-force deviations caused by spindle thermal deformation, a model predictive control method combining a backpropagation (BP) neural network and a genetic algorithm (GA), termed BP-GA, is proposed. Experiments show that the proposed method reduces force-tracking errors compared with dynamics-based feedforward control and maintains consistent force-tracking accuracy under different operating conditions. Finally, staged on-machine loading tests with simulated cutting forces are conducted to provide a preliminary analysis of changes in machine tool geometric accuracy under dynamic loading.

papers.title: Numerical analysis of bone cell growth potential in beam-based lattice structures
papers.abstract: Porous structures have been shown to possess considerable potential for promoting bone regeneration. This capacity is attributable to the ability of such structures to emulate the mechanical and biological environment of natural bone. These cells have been shown to promote cell adhesion, proliferation, and nutrient transport, which renders them particularly well-suited for applications in tissue engineering. The present study evaluates four beam-based lattice structures -Cubic Body-Face Centered Cubic (CBFCC), Cubic Face-Centered Cubic (CFCC), Kelvin, and Octet Truss- in terms of their geometric and flow-related properties to assess their suitability for bone regeneration. Scaffolds with porosities of 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80% were modeled to investigate the effects of geometry. To this end, numerical analyses were conducted under laminar flow conditions to evaluate permeability, wall shear stress (WSS), and flow velocity. The findings of the study suggest a correlation between increasing porosity and the following outcomes: increased flow inlet areas, reduced pressure drops, and enhanced permeability. The observed scaffold permeability values were found to fall within the range reported for human trabecular bone, thereby supporting effective nutrient transport and metabolic waste removal. WSS analysis revealed that 30.28% to 74.64% of the scaffold surfaces were within the optimal range of 10–30 mPa, which is conducive to bone cell development. The flow velocities remained within physiological laminar limits, thereby ensuring appropriate mechanical stimulation and uniform flow distribution throughout the scaffolds. In summary, the beam-based lattice architectures exhibited a balanced relationship between structural characteristics and flow performance. This study provides a comprehensive evaluation of their potential for bone regeneration and establishes a foundation for future experimental validation.

papers.title: Fibrous interface formation in a hydroxyapatite patient-specific implant after maxillomandibular advancement: histological and μCT insights from a case report
papers.abstract: Maxillomandibular rotational advancement (MMA) is an established treatment for patients with severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but sufficient ossification at the Le Fort I osteotomy gap remains challenging, particularly in large advancements. This study evaluated the in vivo integration pattern and clinical feasibility of a patient-specific hydroxyapatite implant (HA-PSI) used for augmentation of the Le Fort I osteotomy gap in MMA. A 35-year-old patient with severe OSA (AHI: 60/h) underwent MMA with 7.2 mm anterior advancement of the maxilla and placement of HA-PSI on the Le Fort I osteotomy gaps bilaterally. After 9 months during secondary surgery for plate removal and genioplasty, site-specific biopsies were obtained and analyzed using histology and micro-computed tomography (μCT). Combined histological and histomorphologic analysis revealed close spatial adaptation between native bone and the HA-PSI without direct bone–implant contact. A thin fibrous connective tissue interface without inflammatory or foreign-body reactions indicated a biologically tolerated integration. HA-PSIs showed feasible and well-tolerated integration in the Le Fort I osteotomy gap, characterized by a stable fibrous interface rather than direct bone contact under functional loading conditions. Further investigations in larger cohorts and comparative studies are warranted.

papers.title: DIGITAL DESIGN OF TITANIUM CAGES AS A STAGE IN OPTIMIZING THE RECONSTRUCTION OF SEGMENTAL BONE DEFECTS
papers.abstract: Large segmental bone defects caused by high-energy trauma require simultaneous restoration of anatomical geometry, mechanical stability and conditions for bone regeneration. Titanium cages with controlled porous architecture represent a promising reconstructive option. Modern digital technologies make it possible to move consistently from computed tomography data to a three-dimensional bone model, perform virtual reduction, create a CAD model of the cage, modify its geometric parameters and conduct preliminary biomechanical assessment. This paper reviews the digital workflow of titanium cage design and demonstrates it using a humeral bone-defect reconstruction example. Particular attention is paid to generating several design variants with different structural densities and pore sizes. Such an approach allows potentially favorable configurations to be selected before physical manufacturing by balancing mechanical support and open space for bone regeneration. Further integration of digital modelling, mechanical testing and in vivo experiments may provide a basis for determining cage parameters that optimize osseointegration.

papers.title: Surrogate-Based Numerical Optimization of Buried PVC Pipes Beneath Strip Footings on Sand Slopes
papers.abstract: Pipes along slopes often run beneath shallow foundations. This numerical study examines how the burial depth and flexural stiffness of a buried PVC pipe govern its response beneath a strip footing on a sand slope. A PLAXIS 2D model validated against the footing response in nine reduced-scale model tests was used for 390 analyses covering slope angles of 20–35°, footing setbacks b/B = 0–1, burial depths H/D = 1–4 and pipe stiffness ratios EI/EI0 = 0.25–4. Pipe ovalization decreased six- to tenfold with depth and stiffness and increased with slope angle, while service wall stresses remained well below the design stress of PVC. Pipes buried shallower than about two footing widths reduced the bearing capacity, although the model underestimated this reduction relative to the tests. Gaussian process surrogates predicted the pipe response accurately (R2 ≥ 0.999) but the bearing capacity ratio (BCR) only moderately (R2 = 0.73, and 0.38 for unseen slope–setback combinations); a safety margin was therefore applied to the BCR constraint, and three of the resulting optimal designs satisfied it in independent finite element analyses. With only two design variables and a simplified relative cost index, GA, PSO and DE outperformed random sampling only for the constrained single-objective problem.

papers.title: On analytical evaluation of radial and bending stiffness of transcatheter aortic valve stent lattice structure
papers.abstract: Background and Objective Mechanical performance of transcatheter aortic valve stents (radial and bending stiffness) primarily depends on their geometry and cell architecture. Finite element simulations and experimental testing of these cellular lattice structures are computationally expensive and unsuitable for quick design optimization, especially for patient-specific devices, which can be additively manufactured. In order to predict the radial and bending stiffness of TAVI stents directly from the parametric lattice shape, an analytical framework must be developed. Methods The TAVI frame was represented parametrically. A periodic diamond cellular lattice made up of circular struts was used to depict the stent. The elastic strain energy related to strut bending and axial deformation was calculated using Castigliano’s second theorem and Euler-Bernoulli beam theory. In order to produce an equal bending stiffness for global bending, the strain energy that resulted from projecting the macroscopic curvature onto the local deformation of each lattice cell/strut was homogenized. The force-displacement response for compression between parallel rigid plates was obtained from the derivative of the total strain energy with respect to the prescribed displacement, and the imposed plate displacement was connected to the deformation of the diamond lattice. TAVI lattice specimens were mechanically tested to compare the analytical predictions. Results The TAVI lattice geometry and its global mechanical response were found to be explicitly related by the analytical formulation. Strut diameter, lattice topology, circumferential cell number, axial cell number, and local strut length all significantly influenced the anticipated bending stiffness; the bending-dominated contribution scaled with the fourth power of strut diameter. The effects of lattice bending and axial strut deformation to the force-displacement response were also included in the plate-compression equation. The main patterns seen in the experimental observations were replicated by the analytical framework. Conclusion The proposed analytical approach can be adopted for geometry optimization and patient-specific TAVI frame design. A useful application of this theoretical approach is additive manufacturing of these stents by adjusting stent design to meet particular clinical and anatomical needs to find a balance between radial stiffness, bending flexibility, and structural performance.

papers.abstract: Introduction: Total hip arthroplasty (THA) is associated with substantial perioperative blood loss and allogeneic transfusion requirements. Tranexamic acid (TXA), a synthetic antifibrinolytic agent, may reduce these complications, although its routine use remains inconsistent across healthcare settings. Materials and methods: This prospective, single-center comparative study included 80 patients undergoing primary uncemented THA for coxarthrosis at the University Clinic for Orthopedic Diseases in Skopje (2023–2025). Forty patients received 1 g intravenous TXA before skin incision, while 40 served as controls. Total blood volume and blood loss were calculated using the Nadler and Mercuriali formulas, respectively. Statistical analysis included Student's t-test, chi-square test, and repeated-measures ANOVA (p<0.05). Results: Both groups were comparable regarding demographic characteristics and preoperative hematological parameters. TXA significantly reduced total blood loss (1327.92±553.6 vs. 2144.47±727.4 mL, p<0.001), erythrocyte volume loss (486.05±198.5 vs. 765.07±254.7 mL, p<0.001), and drain output (564.45±210.7 vs. 679.80±207.6 mL, p=0.016). Transfusion requirements were substantially lower in the TXA group (9 vs. 39 units). Hemoglobin and hematocrit levels were also significantly higher from three hours postoperatively. No thromboembolic events were observed. Conclusion: A single preoperative 1 g intravenous dose of TXA significantly reduces perioperative blood loss, drainage, and transfusion requirements following uncemented THA, without observed thromboembolic complications. These findings support its routine inclusion in perioperative blood management protocols.

papers.title: Polysaccharide-based graft copolymers as advanced biomaterials: molecular design, functional tailoring, and biomedical applications
papers.abstract: Polysaccharide graft copolymers are becoming versatile biomaterials with unique structural and functional properties. Nevertheless, controlling these polymers is difficult and achieving reliable biomedical devices relies on a number of factors including polymer backbone chemistry, grafting techniques, polymer architecture and biological factors. This review will discuss the mechanism, structure, properties and function of polysaccharide graft copolymers. Starch, cellulose, chitin, chitosan and alginate polymers will be discussed along with poly(ε-caprolactone), polyethylene glycol, polypropylene glycol and poly(vinyl alcohol). Different chemical modification and grafting methods were considered including free radical, cerium ion, reversible deactivation radical, ring opening and click chemistry. Each of these methods will be compared to understand how they work, the advantages and disadvantages, and how they can control the polymer architecture. A particular focus will be on how the degree of substitution, graft density, graft chain length, molecular weight, crystallinity and hydrophilic-hydrophobic balance can affect the swelling behavior, mechanical properties, degradation, self-assembly and biological properties. Examples show that grafting relationships are often non-linear, showing that optimum polymer architectures usually give better results than higher grafting levels. Applications have been looked at including controlled drug and gene delivery, wound healing, tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, smart systems, nanomedicine and 3D bioprinting. Covalent graft copolymers are discussed rather than blends, composites and interpenetrating networks. Challenges include the difficulty controlling the polymer structure, reliability, leftover reagents, long-term safety, green synthesis, scale up and translation into real world applications. Challenges in the future include understanding how to characterize the polymer architecture, modeling structure property relationships and designing polymers for specific applications. With this information this provides a rational approach toward creating reliable, multifunctional and applicable polysaccharide graft biomaterials.

papers.title: Slot-targeted longitudinal unicortical femorotomy for the extraction of an incarcerated femoral intramedullary nail during hip arthroplasty: a case report
papers.abstract: Background Removal of an incarcerated femoral intramedullary nail (IMN) can be technically challenging, particularly when bone ingrowth into a longitudinal slot mechanically locks the implant to the surrounding femur. We describe a slot-targeted longitudinal unicortical femorotomy (STLUF) technique that facilitates controlled removal of an incarcerated slotted femoral IMN during hip arthroplasty. Case presentation A 57-year-old man presented with a femoral neck fracture and a femoral IMN implanted approximately 29 years prior to presentation for a proximal femoral shaft fracture. Preoperative radiography and computed tomography (CT) showed a healed femoral fracture with extensive osseous remodeling and substantial bony ingrowth into the longitudinal slot of the IMN, resulting in the mechanical incarceration of the nail. Based on preoperative CT assessment of the orientation and extent of the longitudinal slot, STLUF was performed through a posterolateral approach. The osteotomy was directed along the slot, which facilitated sequential removal of the ingrown bone and release of the osseous interlock under direct visualization. The nail was subsequently removed, and bipolar hemiarthroplasty was performed. The incarcerated IMN was successfully removed without the need for additional cortical windows, nail transection, substantial cortical damage, or iatrogenic femoral fracture. Conclusion CT-planned STLUF enabled intact removal of a femoral IMN retained for 29 years, followed by bipolar hemiarthroplasty. The patient regained independent ambulation without documented complications. This technique may represent a feasible option for selected cases of suspected slot-related osseous incarceration.

papers.title: Relationship between cortical bone thickness and failure load in the mouse tibia tested in different loading directions
papers.abstract: Introduction The cortical thickness (Ct.Th) of the mouse tibia midshaft is a good predictor of the failure load (FL_FE). Validated micro-computed tomography (micro-CT)-based micro-finite element (micro-FE) models have shown that the loading direction affects the FL_FE. Our aim in this study was to investigate whether Ct.Th is a good predictor of FL_FE under varying loading directions in ovariectomised mice, half of which were subjected to external mechanical loading over a two-week period. Methods The tibiae of eleven ovariectomised C57BL/6 mice at ages 18 and 20 weeks were scanned with micro-CT. Six of the mice underwent external, controlled mechanical loading to stimulate bone apposition at age 19 weeks. The Ct.Th was measured in the bone midshaft (1-mm thick region). Micro-FE models were generated based on segmented micro-CT images. Three models using unitary loads were linearly combined to simulate a range of loading directions spanning different tilt angles from the inferior–superior axis and different azimuthal rotations around the inferior–superior axis, leading to 504 loading directions per mouse at each time point. The minimum principal strain was calculated and used to estimate the failure load by linearly scaling the resultant strain until 10% of the nodes reached the critical strain level of −14,420 με. Linear mixed-effects models were fitted to investigate the correlation between Ct.Th and FL_FE at each loading direction. Results Ct.Th was strongly correlated with FL_FE across all tested loading directions (R 2 m range: 74%–92%), but following False Discovery Rate-correction, only 57 of the 504 loading directions remained significant (q < 0.05). This means that Ct.Th was a strong statistically significant predictor of FL_FE in only 11% of all the loading cases examined. These significant loading directions formed a regional range of loading parameters within the loading cone that incorporated the loading direction associated with the strongest predictive relationship (θ = 10°, ϕ = 200°, R 2 m = 92%). In comparison, the nominal axial loading direction (θ = 0°, ϕ = 0°) had an R 2 m of 86%. Discussion These results indicate that Ct.Th may serve as a practical surrogate estimation of FL_FE, saving computational resources, as long as any loading direction deviations from the nominal axial loading direction fall within this significant regional parameter range.

papers.title: Design and Additive Manufacturing of a Novel Porous Alumina Orbital Implant by Vat Photopolymerization
papers.abstract: Orbital implants are well-established devices for restoring orbital volume after enucleation or evisceration, with porous architecture being widely investigated to promote fibrovascular tissue ingrowth. However, ceramic additive manufacturing for fabricating complex porous orbital implants remains unexplored. This study investigated the feasibility of fabricating porous alumina orbital implants with a stochastic architecture derived from a micro-computed tomography (micro-CT)-based digital model by using vat photopolymerization (VPP). Specifically, a porous structure obtained from a commercial polyurethane sponge was digitally adapted into a spherical implant incorporating a perforated external shell and a planar basal surface. The implant was fabricated using a commercial photocurable alumina slurry and a Lithoz CeraFab 7500 digital processing system. The fabricated implant retained its designed architecture after debinding and sintering, showing an open porosity of around 60%. The final dimensions remained close to the nominal CAD geometry, while scanning electron microscopy analysis confirmed a consolidated alumina microstructure with a mean grain size of 10.44 ± 5.17 µm. These results demonstrate, for the first time, the feasibility of combining micro-CT-derived stochastic architectures with ceramic VPP to fabricate complex porous alumina orbital implant prototypes.

papers.title: A surrogate-model-based blade tuning method for independent control of modal frequencies in aero-engine compressor blades
papers.abstract: Vibration-induced high-cycle fatigue remains a critical constraint on aero-engine compressor blade reliability and safety. Conventional blade tuning relies on iterative aerodynamic and structural adjustments to eliminate resonance risks, suffering from low efficiency and the potential to introduce unintended modal coupling. This study proposes a rapid, surrogate-model-based blade tuning methodology from a structural design perspective. By directly manipulating the cross-sectional coordinates of the airfoil profile, key geometric parameters—primarily the maximum sectional thickness—are precisely modified. A Taylor-series expansion is employed to establish an explicit functional mapping between sectional thickness variations and the first six modal frequencies. A second-order surrogate model, calibrated via least-squares regression on an 8848-sample training set, achieves R 2 = 0.9953–0.9971 with MAPE of 0.10%–0.57% on an independent 1027-sample test set. Parametric studies across the root, middle, and tip regions unveil distinct sensitivity mechanisms, providing the physical foundation for independent modal-frequency control. The tuning task is subsequently reformulated as a constrained optimization problem, which is transformed into a solvable standard-form nonlinear program through objective linearization and constraint relaxation. Finite element validation of 36 optimal schemes confirms that the proposed method achieves (i) precise tuning of target modes (frequency shift >2%) and (ii) controlled management of non-target modes (fluctuation confined within ±0.5%). The entire workflow replaces the conventional empirically driven trial-and-error loop with one-time surrogate construction plus one-time optimization solving, reducing the design cycle from days to minutes. This methodology establishes an efficient and systematic framework for aero-engine compressor blade tuning, providing engineers with a powerful tool to address complex vibration challenges.

This study investigates the biological properties of its modified form—calcium-deficient hydroxyapatite (DHA). Using mechanochemistry, nanocrystalline powders of DHA and zinc, magnesium, and silicon co-substituted DHA were synthesized. The obtained materials were characterized using SEM, XPS, FTIR, and PXRD methods. The samples were implanted into a rat calvarial defect in powder form. Notably, at 4 months post-implantation, particles of ion-substituted DHA were detected within the newly formed bone matrix rather than exclusively within the fibrous scar tissue. By 5 months, no residual granules were observed in either experimental group. papers.title: Mechanical Anisotropy of Metal Alloys Fabricated by Laser Powder Bed Fusion: Effects of Build Orientation, Loading Conditions, and Post-Processing
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) is an additive manufacturing technology that enables the production of metallic components with complex geometries. However, its layer-by-layer melting and rapid solidification processes can generate direction-dependent microstructures and mechanical properties. This review examines the mechanical anisotropy of four representative LPBF alloy systems: Ti-6Al-4V, 316L stainless steel, AlSi10Mg, and Inconel 718. The effects of build orientation, loading conditions, microstructural characteristics, and post-processing are discussed, with emphasis on tensile behavior, fatigue performance, fracture and crack propagation, and high-temperature mechanical response. The reviewed studies indicate that anisotropy results from the combined effects of crystallographic texture, grain morphology, solidification structures, process-induced defects, residual stress, and surface condition. Their relative contributions vary among alloy systems and depend on manufacturing and testing conditions. Furthermore, tensile anisotropy does not necessarily predict fatigue or fracture anisotropy because different loading modes interact differently with defects and microstructural interfaces. Post-processing methods, including heat treatment, hot isostatic pressing, recrystallization, and surface treatment, can modify mechanical properties and directional differences. However, improvements in average mechanical properties do not necessarily indicate the elimination of anisotropy. Finally, current limitations in orientation reporting, defect characterization, and multiscale modeling are identified. This review highlights the importance of integrated experimental and numerical approaches for the reliable design and qualification of LPBF-manufactured metal components.

papers.abstract: Introduction: Intravenous tranexamic acid (TXA) reduces blood loss and transfusion requirements in total hip arthroplasty (THA), but whether age, body mass index (BMI), and sex modify its effect or independently influence perioperative bleeding remains unclear. This secondary analysis investigated associations between these demographic factors and perioperative outcomes. Materials and methods: This hypothesis-generating secondary analysis included 80 patients from a prospective comparative study of primary uncemented THA: 40 received 1 g intravenous TXA before incision and 40 served as controls. Within each group, associations of age and BMI with hematological and blood-loss outcomes were assessed using Pearson correlation, while sex-based differences were evaluated using Student’s t-test and chi-square test. Statistical significance was set at p<0.05. Results: In the TXA group, age correlated with total drain volume (r=0.355, p=0.025) but not with other outcomes. In controls, age correlated with preoperative hemoglobin (r= 0.326, p=0.040), but not with postoperative or blood-loss outcomes. BMI was not significantly associated with any outcome in either group. In controls, males had greater total drain volume than females (769.6±189.0 vs. 590.1±189.1 mL, p=0.005); this difference was not significant with TXA (627.5±234.8 vs. 507.4±172.5 mL, p=0.071). No demographic factor significantly predicted transfusion. Conclusion: Age, BMI, and sex showed limited and inconsistent associations with perioperative bleeding and did not predict transfusion. TXA efficacy appeared broadly consistent across demographic subgroups, although larger adequately powered studies are required to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Physically anchored multi-resolution neural operator framework for flood inundation prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate flood inundation modeling using high-resolution hydrodynamic simulations is computationally demanding, limiting their use for large-scale analysis and rapid scenario evaluation. Although machine learning surrogates have been developed, many struggle to reproduce the full spatiotemporal evolution of flood dynamics while maintaining physically meaningful behavior across spatial scales. In particular, simultaneously capturing basin-scale wave propagation and fine-scale inundation boundaries remains challenging. This study presents a multi-resolution deep learning framework for rapid shallow water equation surrogate emulation of flood depth and extent fields. The approach combines a coarse-resolution neural operator that captures large-scale hydrodynamic behavior with a terrain-aware refinement module that reconstructs fine-scale inundation boundary structure. The framework is trained on high-fidelity two-dimensional shallow-water simulations and evaluated across riverine, dam-break, and complex floodplain systems, including tests under structured bathymetric uncertainty. Results demonstrate accurate reconstruction of continuous water depth fields, wet–dry delineation, and peak flood magnitude and timing. The model closely reproduces the evolution of domain-integrated water volume over time, providing a volume-consistency diagnostic beyond purely geometric agreement, and maintains probabilistic consistency when input topography is uncertain. The framework therefore provides high-resolution surrogate predictions of solver-generated flood depth and extent fields at substantially reduced computational cost relative to direct high-resolution simulation. These findings show that multi-resolution deep learning can efficiently emulate solver-generated hydrodynamic flood responses with strong depth and boundary accuracy and robustness to geometric uncertainty, supporting scalable flood hazard assessment and rapid scenario evaluation.

papers.title: Rapid Discrimination of Different Stir-Frying Degrees of Wine-Moistened Angelica sinensis and Prediction of Marker Compounds Using Multimodal Data Fusion and Intelligent Algorithms
papers.abstract: Angelica sinensis (AS) is a traditionally edible aromatic botanical whose wine-stir-frying degree is largely judged by subjective sensory characteristics. We developed a multimodal framework integrating machine vision, an electronic eye, a flash gas chromatography electronic nose, and Fourier transform near-infrared (FT-NIR) spectroscopy to evaluate wine-processed Angelica sinensis (WAS). Sixteen independent raw-material batches were sampled at 13 time points, including an untreated control (0 min) and 12 sampling points during stir-frying (6–28 min), yielding a total of 208 batch–time-point samples. Feature-level data fusion and intelligent optimization enabled four-class processing-state discrimination and prediction of ferulic acid, ligustilide, senkyunolide I, and coniferyl ferulate contents. Color, texture, odor-related responses, and marker contents showed distinct processing trends. Discriminant functions and preliminary reference ranges quantified appearance characteristics previously assessed empirically. The tree-structured Parzen estimator-optimized random forest (TPE-RF) achieved 98.08% accuracy and a macro-F1 of 0.9833 under repeated batch-grouped cross-validation. Multiobjective Bayesian optimization-assisted partial least squares regression (MOBO-PLSR) yielded R2 values of 0.9371, 0.9357, 0.8899, and 0.9243, respectively, outperforming FT-NIR-only models. Modality analysis highlighted complementary odor and machine-vision information. External validation using three additional batches achieved 94.87% classification accuracy, while regression R2 ranged from 0.7411 to 0.9196. This approach supports objective, quantitative assessment of wine-stir-frying quality.

papers.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Contemporary Statistical Data Analysis: Opportunities and Challenges
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology in modern statistical data analysis, offering innovative approaches to data processing, statistical modelling, prediction, classification and interpretation. The increasing availability of large-scale, complex and multidimensional datasets has created a demand for advanced analytical techniques capable of identifying hidden patterns, relationships and trends beyond the conventional capabilities of traditional statistical methods. AI-based approaches, particularly Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning, Artificial Neural Networks, Natural Language Processing and automated predictive modelling, have significantly expanded the scope of statistical investigation. This paper examines the application of artificial intelligence in contemporary statistical data analysis, highlighting its methodological contributions, practical opportunities and associated challenges. It particularly discusses the integration of AI with conventional statistical techniques, automated data management, predictive analytics, statistical inference, model accuracy, interpretability, and data quality, algorithmic bias and ethical considerations. The study is based on a descriptive and analytical review of relevant academic literature, research publications and institutional reports. The discussion indicates that AI can improve analytical efficiency, computational capacity, predictive accuracy and the ability to analyse complex datasets. However, challenges relating to data representativeness, model transparency, uncertainty quantification, privacy, reproducibility and the distinction between statistical prediction and causal explanation remain significant. The paper claims that artificial intelligence should complement rather than replace conventional statistical methodology. An integrated framework combining statistical reasoning, computational intelligence and human expertise is essential for ensuring reliable, interpretable and scientifically valid statistical outcomes.

The FTIR spectrum disclosed a wide range of functional groups like aliphatic amines, amides (C-N), phenols (O-H) and alkane (C-H) that are responsible for capping and stability of NF-ZnO NPs. The SEM and TEM analyses also confirmed the same with polydispersed NF-ZnO NPs. NF-ZnO NPs exhibited significant antioxidant and antidiabetic activity. NF-ZnO NPs also showed substantial anti-bacterial activity against tested bacteria and anticancer properties against liver (HepG2) and lung (A549) cell lines, reducing their viability in a dose-dependent manner. Furthermore, the current research substantiates that green synthesis might assist in eco-friendly biofabrication of NF-ZnO NPs with potential applications in the fields of medicine and industry.

The activity involved 18 teachers, comprising 8 men and 10 women, and applied an active learning and mentoring approach through preparation, workshop, practice, mentoring, and evaluation stages. papers.title: QPI-Twin: a data re-uploading quantum physics-informed surrogate for anisotropic rotor-bearing systems across a variable speed and load envelope
papers.abstract: Introduction A rotor-bearing digital twin must be physically faithful over a broad envelope of shaft speed, radial load, and bearing health; it must be compact enough for online refinement and embedded storage; and it must extrapolate to operating regimes in which no measurements have been taken. Data-driven diagnostic models satisfy the second requirement but not the third, whereas classical physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) satisfy the first and third only at a large parameter cost. Methods We propose QPI-Twin, in which the equations of motion of an anisotropic Jeffcott rotor on rolling-element supports are imposed as a residual penalty on a data re-uploading parameterised quantum circuit (PQC). The bearing stiffness follows the cube-root Hertzian load law, depends mildly on shaft speed, and is scaled by a health index that represents raceway spalling, so that a single surrogate is valid over the entire speed, load, and health envelope. The angle-encoding weights are initialised with the damped natural frequencies and synchronous forcing rates of the linearised rotor, placing the machine spectrum inside the model hypothesis class before training. The trained surrogate serves as the measurement model of an unscented Kalman filter (UKF) for remaining useful life (RUL) estimation. Results Under a matched budget of 2400 Adam optimiser steps, a 178-parameter quantum trunk achieves 24.8% normalised root-mean-square error (NRMSE) in seen regimes, compared with 42.1% for a size-matched 182-parameter PINN, and is statistically indistinguishable from an 8770-parameter PINN. Removing the physics residual from an otherwise identical model widens the seen-to-unseen gap from 11.9 to 42.9 percentage points, identifying the residual, not the architecture, as the source of transfer. Over 2 to 6 qubits, the slope of log10 physics-residual gradient variance against qubit count is −0.21 under random initialisation, against a barren-plateau prediction of −0.301, and +0.21 under physics-guided initialisation. At this training budget, the UKF-coupled surrogate does not outperform supervised RUL regressors. Discussion This shortfall arises from surrogate fidelity as a measurement model, not from the filter, and is reported rather than omitted. All results are simulated, and the parameter-efficiency and trainability findings hold only within the tested training budget, qubit range, and optimiser.

papers.abstract: This study proposed a novel inverse analysis method for acoustic tomography (ATom) that integrates physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) to reconstruct indoor airflow velocity and temperature fields. The effectiveness of the method was evaluated through numerical experiments using computational fluid dynamics simulations to determine the mean airflow velocity and temperature distributions within a two-dimensional indoor space. The PINN method successfully captured room-scale circulation and temperature distributions. In the base case, a root-mean-square error (RMSE) was below 5% of the supply airflow velocity or temperature difference for all primary variables, and R2 (coefficient of determination) was 0.96 for the velocity component parallel to the primary supply airflow. In contrast to the conventional simultaneous iterative reconstruction technique (SIRT), which was limited by cell resolution, PINNs provided fine-grained distributions and resolved subcellular scales, including near-wall velocity decay. Despite the absence of explicit inlet boundary conditions, the model reproduced the high-velocity, low-temperature characteristics of the supply airflow and the temperature rise near the heated floor. Incorporating physical equations significantly improved reconstruction quality, especially for the velocity component orthogonal to the primary supply airflow. Furthermore, increasing the number of transmitter-receiver pairs enhanced spatial accuracy for the velocity component and temperature.

papers.title: 3D Mineral Prospectivity Mapping Using CNN–CBAM with Uncertainty Quantification: A Case Study from Northwestern Iran
papers.abstract: In recent years, the integration of deep learning techniques into mineral prospectivity mapping (MPM) has significantly improved predictive accuracy; however, most existing models fail to quantify the uncertainty associated with their predictions. This omission is critical because unquantified uncertainty can lead to overconfident exploration decisions, increasing financial and operational risks. This study proposes a novel three-dimensional (3D) MPM framework that integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), and uncertainty quantification (UQ). The model was trained on 12 geological, geochemical, and geophysical data layers within a 10×10×10 m voxel grid in the Siahcheshmeh gold deposit. It combines these datasets to improve prediction accuracy and quantify both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties. Monte Carlo Dropout (MCD) and a UQ-based Random Forest (UQRF) were employed to evaluate predictive confidence and assess uncertainty propagation. The proposed CNN–CBAM–UQ model outperformed baseline models, achieving 97.5% accuracy and 0.95 ROC-AUC. Uncertainty maps and accuracy–rejection curves provided deeper insights into model confidence, enabling more reliable exploration targeting. The integration of UQ with deep learning offers a transparent and risk-aware framework for mineral exploration, supporting more efficient and informed decision-making in complex geological environments.

papers.title: Elasmobranch Use in Biotechnological Applications: Balancing Conservation and Innovation
papers.abstract: Elasmobranchs, including sharks, rays, and skates, are an important source of bioactive compounds with growing relevance to the biotechnology, food, cosmetics, pharmaceutical, and biomedical industries. This systematic review evaluates the use of elasmobranch by-products over the last decade, with particular emphasis on collagen, gelatin, hydrolysed peptides, glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), oils, and other bioactive molecules, while also addressing the conservation status of the targeted elasmobranch species. A PRISMA-guided literature survey identified 110 eligible studies published between 2016 and 2026 from Scopus, PubMed, and Web of Science databases. The reviewed literature shows the broad applicability of elasmobranch-derived compounds in wound healing, tissue engineering, 3D bioprinting, immunotherapy, cosmetic formulations, functional foods, anti-obesity therapies, and environmental monitoring. Collagen and collagen-derived peptides were the most frequently studied biomolecules because of their biocompatibility, bioactivity, and favourable techno-functional properties. Chondroitin sulfate and shark-derived oils also showed high industrial relevance. However, our synthesis also reveals a major disconnect between biotechnological exploitation and conservation: sustainability considerations remain poorly integrated into species selection and sourcing strategies. Species are often selected based on local availability, fish market supply, or bycatch recovery rather than explicit sustainability criteria, and many currently used or investigated species are classified as Near Threatened, Vulnerable, Endangered, or Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species. This paper discusses potential conflicts between biotechnological exploitation and conservation priorities, highlighting the need for more sustainable sourcing strategies that do not place additional pressure on threatened elasmobranch populations.

papers.title: Dynamic enterprise cash flow risk prediction and simulation based decision support via financial theory constrained graph learning and uncertainty aware reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: Predicting enterprise cash flow risk is important for financial early warning and liquidity management. Existing methods mainly rely on static financial ratios, tabular machine learning, or standard temporal models, and are less explicit in modeling financially plausible relationships among cash-flow-related variables. This paper proposes a financial-theory-constrained dynamic graph learning framework with uncertainty-aware simulation-based decision support for cash-flow deterioration risk prediction. Revenue, accounts receivable, inventory, accounts payable, operating cash flow, short-term debt, cash holdings, current liabilities, and liquidity pressure are represented as graph nodes, while financial structural priors restrict graph learning to economically admissible relationships. A dynamic graph module learns time-varying association patterns, an evidential predictor estimates risk probability and uncertainty, and a rule-constrained reinforcement learning module ranks feasible mitigation strategies for human review in a simulated cash flow environment. Experiments on SEC-CFRisk and SimFin-CFRisk show moderate but consistent improvements, reaching 0.848 AUC, 0.467 PR-AUC, and 0.530 F1 on SEC-CFRisk. Ablation, calibration, robustness, and simulation analyses support the framework under the evaluated settings, while decision-support results are interpreted only as simulation-based auxiliary rankings.

papers.title: Non-parametric robustness validation of safety-shielded decentralised battery dispatch under state-of-charge estimation and actuation uncertainty in distributed energy resources
papers.abstract: Battery dispatch policies for distributed energy resources (DERs) are usually evaluated with a single deterministic simulation, which cannot show whether the reported savings survive the sensing and actuation imperfections of a deployed battery management system. This paper establishes a statistically validated robustness baseline on all seventeen buildings of the public CityLearn Challenge 2022 ( phase_all_plus_evs ) dataset, which combines photovoltaic (PV) capacities of 4–15 kW, seven electric-vehicle (EV)-equipped buildings and a dataset-native battery of 6.4 kWh, 5.0 kW and per-conversion efficiency 0.90. Over a full year of hourly data, a transparent, decentralised self-consumption rule reduces annual district import cost from $17,510.24 to $13,305.24 (24.0%), peak import from 49.06 to 42.18 kW (14.0%) and emissions by 24.8%. Two stochastic variants, each run over 30 independent seeds, isolate sensing error in the believed state of charge (Dispatch-HC) and actuation error in the commanded discharge (Dispatch-RD). Dispatch-HC is practically cost-neutral ($13,305.74 ± $0.27), whereas Dispatch-RD incurs a consistent 2.22% penalty ($13,600.66 ± $2.15); the two cost distributions do not overlap (Mann–Whitney \(U=0\) , \(p\approx 3.0\times 10^{-11}\) ; Cliff’s \(\delta =-1.0\) ), and the actuation error erodes 7.0% of the battery-attributable saving. Formal results prove that both variants remain physically feasible and can never cost more than the no-battery reference, and they explain the asymmetry: sensing error can only withhold energy that remains stored, whereas positive actuation error discharges energy that is exported without value. A per-building analysis shows that reference cost is only weakly related to PV capacity ( \(r=-0.272\) ) and that the lower cost of EV-equipped buildings cannot be separated from their larger PV systems, because every EV-equipped building has more PV capacity than every other building. A controlled synthetic study with the same building specification shows that the actuation penalty grows in proportion to the error magnitude, that a one-hour telemetry delay removes 34% of the saving, and that the rule captures 96% of the perfect-foresight optimum while remaining more robust to forecast error than model predictive control.

papers.title: Low-Level Wind Speed Analysis Methods: A Comprehensive Review and Periodic Table Classification Framework with Reproducible Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Wind speed analysis is highly fragmented, and the current artificial intelligence literature frequently overclaims performance due to inadequate benchmarking. This review introduces a novel “periodic table” framework that organises the field into five methodological families and maps their evolutionary dependencies, revealing critical gaps in data availability and uncertainty quantification. To validate this framework, I critically assess seven methods across three rigorous pillars: a 100-replicate multi-site simulation, 20 years of real-world data from 11 Australian sites, and ungauged spatial estimation. The results dismantle the simplistic narrative that simple methods universally beat complex ones. When meteorological covariates are present, non-linear tree-based models such as BART and XGBoost decisively outperform classical statistical baselines in both accuracy and interval sharpness. However, ARIMA remains highly competitive for univariate point forecasting, despite producing interval widths too wide for operational decisions. Furthermore, spatial ungauged estimation reveals potential instability in ARIMAX models under extrapolation, while decomposition-based hybrids are invalidated by severe data leakage. These findings demonstrate that optimal method selection is entirely context-dependent, necessitating a shift in how models are evaluated. Consequently, reporting rigorous probabilistic metrics, such as the Continuous Ranked Probability Score and prediction coverage, must become standard practice. All reproducible R implementations and datasets are provided online.

papers.title: Natural product-based nanomedicine for precision cancer therapy: integrating AI, digital twins, and multi-omics for clinical translation
papers.abstract: Background Cancer remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with over 18 million new cases and 9.6 million deaths reported annually. Natural products possess anticancer potential but are limited by poor bioavailability, rapid metabolism, and nonspecific distribution. Nanotechnology-based delivery systems enhance targeted delivery, improve bioavailability, and reduce systemic toxicity. This review focuses on how these systems support precision oncology through molecular profiling, biomarker-guided patient selection, and AI-assisted formulation design. Methods A literature search covering January 2021 to August 2026 was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar to identify studies on natural product nanomedicines, cancer therapy, and precision oncology. Records were screened independently by two reviewers in accordance with PRISMA 2020 principles. Results Natural products, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, terpenes, and alkaloids, exhibit anticancer activity against multiple cancers. Nanocarrier-based delivery systems improve their bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy, and AI-assisted formulation optimization is a promising approach. Combination therapies enhance efficacy through synergistic mechanisms, while targeted nanomedicines improve tumor-specific drug delivery and help eliminate cancer stem cells. Despite remaining toxicity, manufacturing, regulatory, and cost challenges, advances in quality-by-design and continuous manufacturing are helping address these barriers. Conclusion Natural product-based nanomedicines are a promising strategy for precision oncology because they enhance efficacy while reducing toxicity. This review is distinguished by its comprehensive integration of biomarker-guided patient selection, AI-assisted formulation design, and emerging digital twin technologies within a unified precision oncology framework—a combination that, to our knowledge, earlier reviews have not addressed jointly. Advances in AI-assisted formulation, targeted drug delivery, and personalized treatment are accelerating clinical translation. However, standardized formulations, comprehensive safety evaluation, large-scale clinical trials, and streamlined regulatory frameworks remain essential to enable clinical adoption and improve global cancer outcomes.

papers.title: Impact of compositional variability of CO2 mixture on pipeline flow under variable operating and design conditions
papers.abstract: Large-scale deployment of carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies involves safe and efficient transport of CO 2 in pressurized pipelines, from industrial facilities to storage sites. Captured CO 2 streams typically contain variable amounts of impurities such as N 2 , O 2 , CH 4 , and H 2 , which can significantly affect thermophysical properties of the CO 2 mixture, altering its phase behavior and pressure and temperature evolution along the pipeline. We investigate the influence of compositional variability of such mixtures on CO 2 transport using Kolmogorov–Arnold networks (KANs). The latter are trained on simulations generated using a one-dimensional Homogeneous Equilibrium Model under varying inlet conditions and pipe geometries. Our numerical experiments demonstrate that KAN surrogates accurately predict the distance at which two-phase conditions first occur, the pressure at that location, and the coefficient characterizing the magnitude of the pressure decay along the single-phase portion of the pipeline, across a wide range of operating and compositional scenarios. A sensitivity analysis reveals the relative impact of individual impurities and operational parameters on the transport behavior. Our framework provides a tool for uncertainty quantification and rapid assessment of CO 2 transport systems under realistic operating conditions, establishing a foundation for studies supporting the reliable scaling of CCS infrastructure.

papers.abstract: Outdoor science education in protected natural areas faces the challenge of connecting geological heritage (geoheritage) and biodiversity with secondary education curricula. This study presents the design and feasibility of an inclusive, technology-enhanced field trip structured around five key stops in the Arribes del Duero Natural Park (Spain) for first-year Compulsory Secondary Education (ESO) students (aged 12–13). The methodology integrates active approaches (experiential learning, cooperative work and Universal Design for Learning, UDL), combining mobile identification apps (Rock Identifier, PlantNet), a field notebook, gamified activities (a biodiversity bingo) and Cardboard-type virtual reality (VR) goggles. To assess its feasibility, a preliminary study was conducted with university students, analysing satisfaction, motivation and recognition. The results showed high overall satisfaction, with the highest scores for digital resources/VR and gamification, as well as high identification rates for key geological and biological elements. The VR preview was well rated by participants and is proposed as a support and inclusion tool for students with special educational needs. This work contributes a scalable three-layer hybrid model (field observation, gamification and VR immersion) aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 4, 10 and 15) to advance inclusive geoeducation.

papers.title: Digital Twin Technology for Pipeline Systems: A Comprehensive Review of Future Perspectives
papers.abstract: Pipelines are vital infrastructure for long-distance energy transportation but remain vulnerable to various threats, including leakage, corrosion, and structural degradation. Traditional monitoring methods often fall short in real-time analysis and data fusion, relying primarily on offline evaluation and reactive maintenance approaches. Digital twin (DT) has recently emerged as a transformative approach to pipeline management by establishing dynamic, bidirectional links between physical systems and their virtual counterparts. This enables continuous monitoring, predictive analytics, and intelligent decision-making. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of DT applications in pipeline systems, examining system architecture, data acquisition and fusion strategies, modeling development, and updating across oil and gas, subsea, and other types of pipelines. It further identifies key challenges related to data fusion, algorithm interpretability, adaptive modeling, uncertainty quantification, and system deployment. Future research directions are outlined to facilitate the practical deployment of DT for enhancing pipeline safety, reliability, and operational efficiency. Additionally, an emerging dynamic Bayesian network–based DT framework is proposed, establishing a promising pathway for advanced DT applications in pipeline systems.

papers.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a leading cause of global disability, and traditional imaging modalities such as X-rays are insensitive to the tissue compartments where exercise acts, such as cartilage composition and synovial activity. This review comprehensively summarizes recent advances in the application of artificial intelligence (AI) combined with highly sensitive and biologically specific imaging techniques (which offer the secondary advantage of being radiation-free), including quantitative MRI and ultrasound, for precise OA monitoring and motion rehabilitation. Although the analytical framework holds translational potential for other joints (e.g., hip and hand), the strict scope of this review is confined to the knee, as it overwhelmingly dominates the current evidence base for AI imaging and biomechanical modeling. By synthesizing existing literature, this review conceptualizes a closed-loop pathway from assessing joint microstructure remodeling—encompassing cartilage, subchondral bone, and synovium—to generating intelligent exercise prescriptions. By analyzing how AI functions as a core “interpreter” to automatically segment images, extract radiomic features, and build predictive models, this article highlights the transformative shift from experience-driven therapy to data-driven personalized intervention. Furthermore, the review explores cutting-edge developments in longitudinal dynamic monitoring, digital twin simulation, and subgroup identification, aiming to provide a scientific foundation for comprehensive, lifecycle joint health management in knee OA patients.

papers.title: Simultaneous physics-informed neural networks for coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical processes in porous media
papers.abstract: Coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) processes in porous media have so far been solved with physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) through sequential training strategies that optimize the networks of each physical field in alternating stages, mirroring classical operator splits. Sequential schemes, however, sever the gradient pathways between fields, and the reported failure of simultaneous training for THM systems has remained unexplained. This paper presents a simultaneous PINN framework with data-free training for coupled THM processes in saturated and unsaturated porous media. The framework is based on an analytical reduction of the governing system before training. The gas-phase mass balance is eliminated based on the high mobility of the gas phase, and the mechanical equations are eliminated through a stress first-integral in one dimension and a potential reduction in two dimensions. As a result, only two networks, for pressure and temperature, remain to be trained. Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed exactly through the network ansatz, the remaining residuals are trained in a single optimization loop under a causal weighting schedule, and a set of auxiliary constraints derived analytically from each problem statement replaces the supervision that reference data would otherwise provide. The framework is evaluated on three benchmarks: non-isothermal consolidation of a saturated soil column, thermoelastic consolidation of an unsaturated stratum, and a two-dimensional extension of the unsaturated problem with a tapered drying boundary, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first two-dimensional two-phase THM configuration examined with a PINN. With no reference values entering any loss term, and with the reference solution used only to select among random initializations, the predicted fields reach relative L 2 errors between 1.7% and 9.9% and coefficients of determination between 0.979 and 0.999 against independent finite element solutions, and the displacement fields, which are not trained, are recovered from the trained pressure and temperature fields with comparable accuracy.

papers.title: MoE-SOP: Sewer Overflow Prevention via Multimodal Mixture of Experts Large Language Model
papers.abstract: Extreme rainfall and rapid urbanization have significantly increased the strain on urban drainage systems, leading to frequent sewer overflow events that pose serious risks to public health, infrastructure, and environmental sustainability. Traditional prevention strategies rely on passive mechanisms that are highly susceptible to dynamic uncertainties, such as sensor noise and inaccurate rainfall predictions, limiting their reliability in real-world deployment. To address these challenges, we propose MoE-SOP, a Multimodal M ixture of E xperts S ewer O verflow P revention Framework, which integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) with a multimodal expert reasoning architecture. MoE-SOP introduces a multimodal perception layer, where specialized expert models process diverse data sources to achieve robust system awareness: (1) the Information Expert leverages LLMs to analyze structured text data, extract critical insights, and generate decision support; (2) the Structural Expert employs a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) to model the spatial topology of the drainage system and enhance resilience against uncertainty through masked training; (3) the Image Expert processes simulator-rendered visual data to detect overflow anomalies. To ensure optimal decision-making, MoE-SOP incorporates a gated expert decision layer, which adaptively fuses insights via an attention-driven mechanism to generate proactive, context-aware control actions. To evaluate its effectiveness, MoE-SOP is tested within a Stormwater Management Model (SWMM) simulation environment under extreme rainfall conditions and high sensor noise. Experimental results show that MoE-SOP reduces overflow volume by 27.3% and maintains 89.7% overflow prevention performance under 20% sensor noise, significantly outperforming reinforcement learning and model predictive control baselines. Our findings highlight the potential of multimodal expert-guided frameworks in enhancing real-time, adaptive urban flood management. Code is available at https://github.com/shentaodeepwave/Moe-SOP.

papers.title: Process Optimization for Sustainable Laser Powder Bed Fusion of Stainless Steel
papers.abstract: Laser Powder Bed Fusion (L-PBF) enables the fabrication of complex components through layer-wise manufacturing, offering significant opportunities for improved material utilization and design flexibility. However, identifying sustainable process conditions remains challenging due to the trade-offs between manufacturing performance, environmental impact, economic cost, and social considerations. This study proposes a quantitative Sustainability Index (SI) framework for the integrated assessment and optimization of L-PBF process parameters. The proposed approach combines performance, environmental, and economic indicators into a single optimization objective, enabling sustainability to be directly incorporated into process parameter selection rather than evaluated only as a post-processing criterion. Social considerations are additionally incorporated through a context-dependent assessment to investigate the influence of geographical manufacturing conditions and stakeholder priorities. An experimental dataset comprising 154 L-PBF-manufactured 304L stainless steel specimens produced under different combinations of laser power, scanning speed, and hatch distance was employed to evaluate the proposed framework. Performance was assessed through density and crystallographic isotropy indicators, while environmental and economic aspects were quantified through operational energy consumption and manufacturing-related costs. Multi-Criteria Decision-Making was used to construct the SI, while a regression-tree-based surrogate model and differential evolution optimization algorithm were employed to identify sustainable processing conditions. The results demonstrate that improved sustainability performance is achieved through parameter combinations involving relatively low laser power, high scanning speed, and increased hatch distance, reducing energy consumption and operational costs while maintaining adequate material quality. The optimization procedure consistently identifies improved solutions under different weighting scenarios. Furthermore, the incorporation of country-specific social indicators reveals the influence of regional conditions and sustainability priorities on the final assessment outcomes. The proposed SI provides a quantitative decision-support framework for sustainability-oriented L-PBF optimization and establishes a transferable methodology for future sustainable additive manufacturing applications.

papers.title: Sedentarismo e tempo de tela em estudantes do ensino superior: uma revisão sistemática
papers.abstract: Sedentary behavior and screen time are relevant aspects of higher education students' daily routines, particularly due to academic activities and the use of electronic devices. This study aimed to analyze the scientific evidence on the relationship between screen time and sedentary behavior among higher education students. A systematic literature review was conducted, with a narrative synthesis of the findings, through searches in the PubMed/MEDLINE, Virtual Health Library (VHL), LILACS, and SciELO databases. Studies published in Portuguese, English, and Spanish were considered according to previously established eligibility criteria. A total of 50 records were identified, of which five studies were included after duplicate removal and application of the selection criteria. The studies indicated a high prevalence of sedentary behavior among university students, associated with academic and occupational activities and the use of electronic devices. They also reported associations involving sleep quality and potential effects of screen time on physical and mental health. Strategies such as movement breaks and physically active learning activities were identified as potential approaches to interrupt prolonged periods of sitting. It is concluded that screen time and sedentary behavior are relevant issues for health promotion in higher education settings. However, the limited number of included studies and the heterogeneity of findings warrant caution when interpreting the evidence and highlight the need for further research.

papers.title: Dual-Envelope Trajectory Planning and Control for Emergency Obstacle Avoidance in Distributed-Drive Electric Vehicles
papers.abstract: Emergency obstacle avoidance near the handling limits requires the vehicle to clear the obstacle and recover for continued driving. This paper presents a trajectory planning and tracking framework based on dual envelopes in the sideslip angle and yaw rate plane. The outer envelope combines front tire saturation limits with nominal arcs evaluated at the steering and yaw moment limits. The planner enforces this envelope as a hard constraint and penalizes inner envelope violations according to the maneuver phase. It jointly optimizes the trajectory, control inputs, and phase durations under constraints on the full vehicle footprint and terminal recovery. A hierarchical controller combines preview model predictive control with robust vehicle motion tracking. At 20 m/s with an obstacle distance of 22 m, and at 24 m/s with a distance of 27 m, the conventional baseline fails the footprint clearance check. The dual envelope planner clears the obstacle and reduces peak sideslip by 59.9% and 26.8%, respectively, compared with planning using only the outer envelope. In hardware in the loop tests of the 22 m case, the root mean square tracking errors in sideslip and yaw rate decrease by 81.9% and 69.4%, respectively.

papers.title: Equilibrated Physics-Informed Neural Networks with Integrated Constitutive Histories for Annular Creep
papers.abstract: Temporal neural approximations of creep must retain independent material memories while keeping their evolution compatible with mechanical equilibrium. We develop an equilibrated integral-history physics-informed neural network for a radial-shear Nishihara model of annular creep. A continuous stress representation generates Kelvin and viscoplastic histories through exact temporal cell integrals at radial nodes. Their spatial antiderivative reconstructs displacement under prescribed boundary histories, enforcing radial equilibrium while positive interpolation preserves irreversible accumulation. Numerical examples resolve the spatial distribution of constitutive history defects and their accumulation under shared mechanical constraints. Under a common rate objective, the integral model reduces the maximum viscoplastic history defect by factors of 36 and 75 at two initializations. The differential model gives smaller Kelvin defects at both. Unloading below yield arrests irreversible flow during Kelvin recovery. With milder unloading, irreversible strain continues to accumulate during recovery. An explicit yield-interpolation defect separates spatial resolution effects from stress compatibility. A coupled energy estimate converts actual constitutive residuals into continuous bounds on both branch states and reconstructed stress without an exponential growth factor. At 200 h the weighted RMS stress difference from an independent finite-difference solution is 0.000582 MPa in the monotonic case, compared with a residual-based stress indicator of 0.0662 MPa.

O objetivo central é discutir o desenvolvimento prático de estratégias bioclimáticas voltadas especificamente para o contexto habitacional do Nordeste brasileiro, utilizando exclusivamente a infraestrutura de laboratório presencial com foco na confecção de maquetes físicas de escala e ensaios experimentais no Heliodon (simulador de trajetória solar). A metodologia pedagógica ancorou-se na Aprendizagem Baseada em Projetos (ABP), desafiando os estudantes a otimizarem a proteção solar e a eficiência térmica passiva de Habitações de Interesse Social (HIS). Os resultados demonstram que a vivência empírica, tátil e presencial no laboratório reduziu drasticamente as taxas de retenção na disciplina, promovendo nos futuros profissionais uma consciência crítica sobre a sustentabilidade e a responsabilidade social da arquitetura e engenharia frente às realidades climáticas severas da região Nordeste. ABSTRACT: This article presents an in-depth report of teaching experience on the teaching-learning process in the Environmental Comfort course of an undergraduate program in Architecture and Urbanism. The central objective is to discuss the practical development of bioclimatic strategies aimed specifically at the housing context of Northeastern Brazil, using exclusively the in-person laboratory infrastructure, with a focus on building scale physical models and conducting experimental tests in the Heliodon (a solar path simulator). The pedagogical methodology was anchored in Project-Based Learning (PBL), challenging students to optimize solar protection and passive thermal efficiency in Social Interest Housing (HIS). The results show that the empirical, tactile, in-person laboratory experience drastically reduced failure rates in the course, fostering in future professionals a critical awareness of sustainability and of the social responsibility of architecture and engineering in the face of the severe climatic realities of the Northeast region. papers.title: Competition between Enthalpy and Entropy in Dynamic Catalysis of Alumina-Supported Pd Nanoclusters
papers.abstract: The catalytic performance of supported metal nanocatalysts is intrinsically linked to their dynamic structural evolution under reaction conditions. However, resolving these rapid, multiscale transitions remains a formidable challenge. Here, we combine an active learning workflow with enhanced sampling molecular dynamics to construct machine-learning potentials to simulate structural dynamics and O2 dissociation on Pd nanoclusters supported on γ-Al2O3 and θ-Al2O3 surfaces. We reveal that strong metal−support interactions significantly alter the phase behavior of Pd clusters: unlike unsupported clusters, which undergo sharp, size-dependent solid−liquid transitions, supported clusters exhibit suppressed fluxionality and lack distinct melting transitions. Despite these structural differences, the free energy of O2 dissociation displays a universal U-shaped temperature dependence across all systems. Thermodynamic decomposition identifies the origin of this profile as competition between enthalpy and entropy that governs the Gibbs free energy: as temperature rises, the enthalpic drive is eventually counterbalanced by an entropic penalty. These findings suggest that the support primarily governs the structural stability and phase behavior of Pd nanoclusters, whereas the intrinsic thermodynamics of O−O bond scission are dictated by the local chemical environment. This work provides atomistic insight into supported nanoparticle catalysis and offers guidance for designing nanocatalysts with improved activity and durability.

papers.title: Towards scalable manufacturing of laminated Perovskite solar cells through automated rolling and Bayesian optimization
papers.abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are traditionally fabricated by sequential deposition of multiple layers, which constrains the materials selection and processing conditions during manufacturing. Lamination offers an alternative strategy to overcome these limitations, wherein two half-stacks are processed separately and joined to form a device. Current demonstrations of laminated PSCs rely on hot pressing, a serial process that could limit throughput. Herein, a customized rolling system was developed that allows for automated control of key lamination process parameters. A Bayesian optimization (BO) workflow was used to study how these parameters affect bond uniformity and to identify processing conditions that improve the bonded area fraction. To make the optimization more relevant to manufacturing, a cost-weighted acquisition function was developed to guide BO toward an acceptable quality threshold while minimizing a user-defined manufacturing cost function. Statistical analysis identified temperature and velocity as critical parameters. These results demonstrate a laboratory-scale proof-of-concept of rolling lamination that provides a pathway toward continuous lamination of PSCs. We also introduce a BO framework tailored to the specific needs and cost models of a manufacturing plant.
