papers.title: Effects of Cross-Sectional Gradient on Damping Performance and Energy Dissipation of LPBF Self-Sealing Powder Dampers
papers.abstract: This study addresses the fabrication difficulty of variable-cross-section structures and the unclear energy dissipation mechanism of micron-scale self-sealing powder dampers. A novel gradient self-sealing powder damper monolithically fabricated via laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) is proposed. Three equal-volume Ti-6Al-4V specimens, including zero-gradient cylindrical, moderate-gradient circular frustum and strong-gradient conical configurations, are tested via sinusoidal swept-sine vibration experiments on a simply supported beam. Experimental results verify the pronounced orientation dependence of the gradient regulation effect. Under axial excitation, the cylindrical cavity delivers stable and robust performance with no failure risk across the full gradient range. Under transverse excitation, the moderate-gradient frustum achieves the maximum equivalent damping ratio of 0.0819, i.e., 3.7 times that of the same specimen under axial excitation, while the regulation intensity of the gradient effect—defined as the spread in the vibration reduction rate across the gradient range—is 4.8 times that under axial excitation. A critical gradient threshold of α* ≈ 0.30, defined as the gradient at which the vibration reduction rate vanishes, is identified (95% confidence interval 0.27–0.32); beyond it, vibration amplification occurs under high-amplitude excitation. The established three-parameter coupled design framework provides quantitative theoretical guidance for the engineering application of LPBF-integrated vibration damping structures.

papers.title: Real-time operating system architectures for automotive adaptive cruise control: Scheduling, multicore interference and ISO 26262
papers.abstract: Adaptive cruise control (ACC) has to produce its outputs at the right time as well as with the right values. This review looks at how real-time operating systems (RTOSs) support ACC, both in production vehicles and in the research literature. Early electronic control units (ECUs) ran OSEK/VDX or the Automotive Open System Architecture (AUTOSAR) Classic OS on microcontrollers. Newer high-performance systems on a chip use AUTOSAR Adaptive, portable operating system interface (POSIX) and microkernel RTOSs, real-time Linux, or hypervisors, and the review follows that move. For each class of platform it covers scheduling, protection and how well it fits the ACC pipeline of sensing, tracking, control and actuation. It then links the choice of control algorithm (proportional-integral-derivative control, model predictive control or cooperative ACC) to real-time cost, summarises results on multicore timing analysis and mixed criticality, and relates them to the freedom-from-interference requirements of ISO 26262. A hypothetical response-time analysis shows how a designer can budget an ACC task set. The review ends with open problems in multicore interference, certification of high-performance platforms and learning-enabled controllers. It is a literature review, and no new experiments were run.

papers.title: A differentiable model based reinforcement learning framework for complex continuous process optimization
papers.abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) has shown considerable potential for complex industrial process optimization. However, applying RL to production decision problems in alumina production remains challenging because high-fidelity mechanistic simulations are computationally expensive, and conventional RL algorithms require large numbers of simulator evaluations. Existing offline RL methods also suffer from extrapolation errors when policies select actions outside the support of historical data. To address these challenges, we propose an offline reinforcement learning framework based on differentiable latent dynamics. The framework learns a robust process-state encoder and a differentiable forward dynamics model from 995 fixed offline transitions, and then optimizes a policy using Backpropagation Through Time over finite-horizon latent trajectories without additional simulator queries. An incremental action-smoothing mechanism maps policy outputs to feasible production-target updates. In a common 50-step SysCAD evaluation, D-LMPO improves hourly profit by 4.39%, compared with 3.01% for MOPO, 2.12% for TD3+BC, and 0.17% for IQL. In an end-to-end query-efficiency comparison, D-LMPO with historical data available attains 105,909.95 within 50 deployment queries, while the highest-scoring online agent, TD-MPC2, reaches 105,240.41 at 1,000 queries. The proposed mapping limits each normalized target change to 5% while retaining essentially the same final profit as direct policy execution. Clinical trial registration Not applicable. This study does not involve a clinical trial.

papers.abstract: CE-QUAL-W2 fills gaps in observations, and LIME explains predictor importance across three depth layers. Plots compare observed water temperature profiles with predictions from tuned LSTM models. Predicting depth-specific reservoir temperatures supports management. This study developed an interpretable long short-term memory (LSTM) framework for Soyang Reservoir, South Korea, to identify informative meteorological predictors and configurations by depth, not deliver operational profile predictions. Approximately 24% of the 45,291 temperature records were missing; these gaps were filled using outputs from a calibrated two-dimensional hydrodynamic model. Automated machine learning (AutoML) optimized hyperparameters; Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) quantified depth-specific input contributions. Under the model representation, LIME identified ground temperature and cloud cover as the most statistically informative predictors in the epilimnion, whereas small-pan evaporation was more informative in the metalimnion and hypolimnion. Bayesian optimization with the top 11–13 LIME-ranked variables matched the full 15-variable configuration's skill, with epilimnetic Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency up to 0.88. Paired tests confirmed that performance differences remained within run-to-run variability. These results identified a parsimonious, depth-informative feature subset rather than an operationally superior model. However, independently trained layer-wise models produced physically inconsistent vertical temperature profiles with discontinuous thermal gradients, indicating that process-guided deep learning constraints are needed. This study provides an automated and interpretable feature-selection and diagnostic workflow that identifies depth-specific meteorological predictors and reveals where physics-guided constraints are required for vertically coherent prediction.

papers.abstract: High-grade iron ore scarcity increases the need for transferable kinetics from standardised reducibility tests. Lump and pellets were investigated under H 2 and CO in 47 ISO-type packed-bed tests varying temperature, particle size, gas composition and product-gas addition. Lump particle-size exponents averaged −1.2 under H 2 and −1.0 under CO, consistent with predominantly interfacial control, while the apparent activation energy under H 2 was approximately 50 kJ mol −1 . Hancock–Sharp exponents varied with conversion, and six mechanism functions provided the best single-step fits. A reduced-order model coupled the Fe 2 O 3 →Fe 3 O 4 →FeO→Fe steps through stoichiometric oxide balances and a common gas-film correction. With a uniform first-order (F1) assignment, the coupled model improved on the best single-step fit in 43 of 47 tests (in-sample). The wüstite-to-iron step supplied most of the modelled rate beyond x ≈ 0.3. The fitted step coefficients varied with particle size, temperature and reductant and were higher under H 2 than CO.

papers.title: Plant-Derived Silver Nanoparticles as Promising Therapeutic Agents in Overcoming the Global Challenge of Antimicrobial Resistance
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance has reached a critical inflection point, with drug-resistant infections directly responsible for over one million deaths annually and projected to cause 1.91 million deaths per year by 2050. The failure of the antibiotic pipeline leaves a therapeutic need for new, non-resistance approaches, especially against ESKAPE pathogens that have evolved multiple mechanisms of resistance, including the ability to produce enzymes that degrade antimicrobials, express increased amounts of efflux pumps that pump the antimicrobials out of the cell, modify target molecules, and thrive in biofilms, which rapidly neutralise any single-mechanism antibiotic. Plants-derived silver nanoparticles hold another approach to this crisis, one that comes in combination with several different fields: ethnomedicine-based phytochemistry and nanotechnology. Phytochemicals such as flavonoids, polyphenols and tannins, play multifunctional roles, such as reducing and capping agents, regulating the size, shape and composition of the organic corona that imparts biocompatibility to the nanoparticles. This combination of modes of action, namely disruption of the membrane, formation of ROS, inhibition of the respiration and arrest of the DNA replication, shows the nanomaterials the multi-target profile, which makes the development of resistance highly improbable. This critical review discusses the phytochemical-based determinants for biofabrication, details the antimicrobial spectrum that is resistant bacteria and fungal pathogens and investigates approaches to surface engineering such as polymer coating and synergistic antibiotic conjugation. Toxicology and regulatory hurdles remain to be overcome before this can be realised in the clinic, while anticancer and wound healing applications are also evaluated.

papers.title: Long-term stability of implant therapy without additional bone augmentation.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Since Brånemark demonstrated that bone can heal in direct apposition to titanium without an intervening fibrous interface, implant design, loading protocols, and success criteria have changed substantially. Many sites once thought to require grafting can now receive implants placed directly into native bone. AIM: To review the biological basis, case selection, surgical execution, and long-term outcomes of implant therapy performed without additional bone augmentation, and to identify the determinants of durable peri-implant stability. KEY CONSIDERATIONS: Surface topography governs the bone response. Polished surfaces (Ra < 0.5 μm) invite fibrous encapsulation, whereas moderately rough surfaces (Ra 1.0-2.0 μm) elicit the strongest bone response; because roughness exposed to the oral environment is associated with plaque retention and peri-implantitis, hybrid designs with a machined coronal collar have become widely adopted. Total stability reflects the transition from mechanical to biological fixation, with a remodeling nadir at 2-6 weeks; interfacial micromotion beyond approximately 50-150 μm precludes osseointegration, so any early or immediate loading protocol has to keep micromotion below that level, either by splinting implants across the arch or, for single implants, through adequate primary stability and controlled occlusion. Short (≤ 6 mm), narrow-diameter (3.3-3.5 mm), and tilted, pterygoid, or zygomatic implants now allow many sites to be treated without grafting. Randomized data up to 10 years show 6 mm implants performing similarly to longer implants placed with sinus floor elevation, whereas the long-term evidence for most other graft-avoiding options is still limited. The thickness of bone left around the implant and the implant diameter should be chosen for the individual site rather than by fixed rules. Age alone is not a contraindication, whereas antiresorptive therapy, uncontrolled diabetes, certain medications, and a history of periodontitis modify risk. Reported long-term outcomes range widely, reflecting heterogeneity in implant design, treatment setting, maintenance, and, critically, the conflation of survival with success. CONCLUSIONS: Implants placed in adequate native bone can remain stable long term, provided marginal bone loss does not progress. Avoiding augmentation is well supported for 6 mm implants in the posterior jaws, for 3.3-3.5 mm narrow-diameter implants, and for tilted distal implants in full-arch treatment. The evidence is less certain for extra-short and mini-implants and for pterygoid and zygomatic implants. Augmentation is still indicated when the implant cannot be placed in a prosthetically correct position within the native bone, or when esthetic aspects require the ridge contour to be rebuilt. Prosthetically guided positioning, cleansable restorative contours, adequate keratinized tissue, and structured maintenance determine outcome.

The Bibliometrix-R package refined 6808 initial records into 4375 unique documents, which were analysed using Biblioshiny. Thematic mapping revealed a transition from early pharmacology to a bioengineering era dominated by the USA and China, with exosomes and 3D bioprinting as high-potential areas. RET has become a fast-growing field, moving towards bioactive tissue engineering, with a future trend towards cell-free therapies, exosomes and 3D bioprinting.
